root_cause.text: Bluetooth socket destructors fail to purge sk_error_queue, causing SKB memory leaks when TX timestamping is enabled via SO_TIMESTAMPING and timestamps are never consumed by userspace or the controller is unexpectedly removed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue)` calls to the socket destructors in hci_sock_destruct(), iso_sock_destruct(), l2cap_sock_destruct(), and sco_sock_destruct(). The CVE description explicitly states that when SO_TIMESTAMPING is enabled, "SKBs may be queued into sk_error_queue and will stay there until consumed. If userspace never gets to read the timestamps, or if the controller is removed unexpectedly, these SKBs will leak." The fix references commit 134f4b39df7b which added TX timestamping support, indicating that the error queue population was introduced without corresponding cleanup logic in socket destructors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak in HCI socket destruction by purging the error queue alongside receive and write queues.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue)` in the `hci_sock_destruct` function, following the existing purges of receive and write queues.
intent_record.how: This ensures that the error queue associated with an HCI socket is properly drained and freed when the socket is being destroyed. Without this, error queue packets would leak memory as the socket is torn down, since the error queue was not being explicitly purged like the other queues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent memory leak by purging the error queue during ISO socket destruction.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue)` in the `iso_sock_destruct` function, following the existing purges of receive and write queues.
intent_record.how: This ensures that the error queue associated with an ISO socket is properly drained and freed when the socket is being destroyed. Without this purge, any pending error packets in the error queue would leak memory or remain allocated after socket destruction.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak in L2CAP socket destruction by purging the error queue alongside receive and write queues.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue)` in the `l2cap_sock_destruct` function, following the existing purges of `sk_receive_queue` and `sk_write_queue`.
intent_record.how: This ensures that when an L2CAP socket is destroyed, all queued error packets are properly freed and removed from memory. Previously, the error queue was not being purged during socket destruction, which could lead to memory leaks if error packets remained queued.

intent_record.intent_summary: Purge the error queue during SCO socket destruction to prevent memory leaks from orphaned error packets.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue)` in the `sco_sock_destruct` function, following the existing purges of receive and write queues.
intent_record.how: This ensures that the error queue associated with an SCO socket is properly drained and freed when the socket is being destroyed. Previously, error queue packets were not being purged during socket destruction, which could lead to memory leaks or orphaned skb objects remaining in the error queue.

commit 709fca500067524381e28a5f481882930eebac88
Author: Nguyen Dinh Phi <phind.uet@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 8 03:04:24 2021 +0800

    Bluetooth: hci_sock: purge socket queues in the destruct() callback
    
    The receive path may take the socket right before hci_sock_release(),
    but it may enqueue the packets to the socket queues after the call to
    skb_queue_purge(), therefore the socket can be destroyed without clear
    its queues completely.
    
    Moving these skb_queue_purge()
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The vulnerability root cause is that socket destructors fail to purge sk_error_queue (and other queues), causing SKB memory leaks. The commit addresses this by: (1) removing the skb_queue_purge() calls from hci_sock_release() which can race with the receive path, and (2) adding a new hci_sock_destruct() callback that purges both sk_receive_queue and sk_write_queue at socket destruction time when nothing can reference the socket anymore. The fix also sets sk->sk_destruct = hci_sock_destruct in hci_sock_create(). This is a fix commit, not a bug-introducing commit. The vulnerable construct (missing queue purging in destructor) is ABSENT in this version because the fix has been applied.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `iso_sock_destruct` function (lines 565-570) only purges `sk_receive_queue` and `sk_write_queue` but does NOT purge `sk_error_queue`. According to the vulnerability root cause, Bluetooth socket destructors fail to purge sk_error_queue, causing SKB memory leaks when TX timestamping is enabled via SO_TIMESTAMPING. The function shows: 'static void iso_sock_destruct(struct sock *sk) { BT_DBG("sk %p", sk); skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_receive_queue); skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_write_queue); }' - it is missing the critical line 'skb_queue_purge(&sk->sk_error_queue);' that would be needed to fix the vulnerability. This is a new socket type being introduced, and it inherits the same vulnerability pattern present in other Bluetooth socket types at this time.
